title: A scale, Home Assistant and a forecast

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine's bathroom scale knew a lot more than his weight. Getting that data out of a phone app turned into a reverse-engineering side project.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, what else does a scale measure?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Renpho bio-impedance scale gives BMI, BMR, body age, fat and muscle estimates, water, protein, visceral fat, and resistance readings per limb. His problem was that it all lived in a siloed app. He wanted it in Home Assistant, next to his other automations.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He forked one. The community project hass-renpho had slowed down, and he needed more entities, so he forked it as hass_renpho. It logs into Renpho's cloud, polls on an interval, and exposes sensors. He picked six hundred seconds, partly because logging in can kick your phone out of the app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He ran APKLeaks on the Android app, which scans the package for hosts, paths and keys. He matched those to the fields already mapped and filled gaps when a dashboard showed unknown after an app update. He treats it as an unstable contract.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There was a network twist too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The integration failed even though the app worked on cellular. It looked like a broken integration but was really IP reputation. A VPN or a proxy setting fixed it. It burned an evening.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A notebook with pandas, scikit-learn and Keras, modelling weight only. An LSTM tuned over five trials landed on fifty-two units. But he lists the flaws himself: random splits on a time series, and an input shape that means the LSTM never really reads a sequence.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Same time of day, same clothes, and watch trends over weeks. A one kilo swing is normal noise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. The full write-up has the dashboards and the caveats.
